analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date and adds a paragraph (head lines ~1293-1298) describing PromptPieceTokenStore.lookup. The paragraph says lookup snapshots all of a request's hits before promoting them between two bounded generations, so a rotation mid-lookup cannot turn later pieces into misses. Token arrays share storage, existing admission and byte bounds still apply, and batches with no old-generation hits skip the promotion pass. The supplied units are base_text excerpts (lines 1612-2428) that do not touch the changed hunk, so I reviewed the patch excerpt and the surrounding base text. The patch is documentation only, with no executable code, config or protocol changes, so it introduces no new attack surface.

The only security-relevant point is that the prompt-piece token cache is scoped by prefix-cache scope. The doc says tokens are reused 'in the same prefix-cache scope', which matches the coordinator-authored cacheSalt isolation in T-041. The doc change does not alter that scoping or the SSD cache tier controls (HMAC names, TTL, KEK), and it does not loosen the account isolation. I cannot verify from the supplied evidence that the described implementation (PromptPieceTokenStore code) preserves per-scope isolation or that the snapshot behavior matches. That implementation is not in this batch. A possible hit/miss timing difference falls within the already accepted SEC-035 same-account oracle. The doc claims no new behavior beyond fixing a lookup correctness issue. No findings. A later pass that sees the Swift change should confirm the snapshot does not leak entries across cache scopes and that the byte bounds remain enforced.
